briefs.scaphoid:
Wrist and Hand Pain and Numbness

snuffbox vs styloid vs thumb base · occult scaphoid fracture · carpal tunnel and its mimics · when not to imageWhere exactly is the tenderness or numbness, and would a negative test change anything?

DiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line

Locate the finding first:

  • Anatomic snuffbox after a fall on the outstretched hand: scaphoid fracture until proven otherwise. A negative film does not rule it out (up to 20 to 25% are occult in week one): thumb spica cast, then re-image in 2 to 3 weeks or MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) now.
  • Radial styloid with a positive Finkelstein test: de Quervain tendinopathy, a clinical diagnosis; no imaging and no labs.
  • Thumb to half the ring finger numb at night, thenar sensation spared (the median nerve's palmar cutaneous branch leaves before the tunnel): carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS); numbness that includes the thenar eminence is a proximal lesion.

A negative test cannot rule out disease when pretest probability is high; when the diagnosis is clinical, a provocative test is positive and there are no red flags, extra testing adds only incidental findings.

Other wrist and hand findings First carpometacarpal (CMC) osteoarthritis – thumb base pain, positive grind test, squared joint, older · Colles fracture – distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation (dinner fork) after a fall · Intersection syndrome – crepitus about 4 cm proximal to the wrist, dorsal; rowers, weightlifters · Trigger finger – catching or locking with a nodule at the A1 (first annular) pulley · Ganglion cyst – soft dorsal wrist mass that transilluminates and fluctuates · Dupuytren contracture – palmar cord and contracture of the 4th and 5th digits; alcohol, diabetes · Disseminated gonococcal infection (cannot miss) – fever, migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis of several sheaths, pustules: NAAT (nucleic acid amplification test) and ceftriaxone · Hand arthritis – rheumatoid spares the DIP (distal interphalangeal) joints and hits MCP (metacarpophalangeal) and PIP (proximal interphalangeal) symmetrically; osteoarthritis hits DIP (Heberden) and PIP (Bouchard); psoriatic hits DIP with dactylitis, nail pitting and pencil-in-cup erosions
Management and treatment
Management ladders
ConditionFirstEscalate to
Scaphoid fracture, presumed (negative film)Thumb spica castDisplaced waist or proximal pole fracture: surgical fixation
De Quervain tendinopathy: abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis, first dorsal compartmentThumb spica splint and an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug)Corticosteroid injection, then first dorsal compartment release
Carpal tunnel syndromeNocturnal neutral wrist splintThenar atrophy: surgical release (motor loss is late: lumbricals 1 and 2, opponens, abductor and flexor pollicis brevis)
Why cast on suspicion Retrograde blood supply – enters distally and runs back to the proximal pole; a missed fracture ends in avascular necrosis and nonunion, worst at the proximal pole · Same risk – femoral head, talus and humeral head (retrograde or tenuous supply)
Practice
  1. 22-year-old man fell on his outstretched hand playing basketball tender in the anatomic snuffbox wrist radiographs with a scaphoid view are negative Pain on gripping; no deformity Afebrile · radial pulse normal · sensation intact → Thumb spica cast and re-image in 2–3 weeks → snuffbox tenderness after a fall is a scaphoid fracture until proven otherwise; up to 20 to 25% are occult in week one: thumb spica cast and re-image in 2 to 3 weeks
  2. 22-year-old man, a professional goalkeeper, has snuffbox tenderness after a fall radiographs negative needs a definitive answer before a match next week Thumb spica cast in place Afebrile · sensation intact → MRI of the wrist → MRI shows an occult fracture immediately when a 2-week wait for repeat films is not acceptable
  3. 22-year-old man has 6 months of wrist pain fell on an outstretched hand last winter, not imaged then tender in the anatomic snuffbox Grip weak and painful Afebrile · radiograph: sclerotic proximal scaphoid with a fracture gap → Avascular necrosis and nonunion → the blood supply runs retrograde to the proximal pole, so a missed fracture ends in avascular necrosis and nonunion
  4. 68-year-old woman fell on her outstretched hand on ice tender over the distal radius, not the snuffbox wrist looks like a dinner fork Radiograph: distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation Afebrile · radial pulse normal → Colles fracture → dorsal angulation of a distal radius fracture after a fall is a Colles fracture; snuffbox tenderness would point to the scaphoid
  5. 24-year-old woman was diagnosed with a scaphoid fracture on MRI fracture line near the end closest to the forearm nondisplaced She asks about the risk of the bone dying Afebrile · sensation intact → Proximal pole → the proximal pole carries the highest avascular necrosis risk: its blood supply arrives last, retrograde from the distal end
  6. 22-year-old man fell from his skateboard onto his outstretched hand tender in the anatomic snuffbox radiograph: displaced fracture through the scaphoid waist No other injury; pain on gripping Afebrile · radial pulse normal → Surgical fixation → a displaced waist or proximal pole fracture goes to surgical fixation; casting is for the presumed fracture with a negative film
  7. 29-year-old woman at 34 weeks of gestation has numb hands tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers shakes her hands to relieve it Thenar sensation spared; no neck pain BP 118/72 mm Hg · mild hand and ankle edema → CTS of pregnancy → numbness of the thumb, index and middle fingers relieved by shaking, with thenar sparing and no neck pain at 34 weeks, is carpal tunnel syndrome of pregnancy: nocturnal splint; it usually resolves after delivery
  8. 48-year-old man has new numbness in both hands at night his rings no longer fit coarse facial features and large hands Shoe size has increased BP 148/92 mm Hg · glucose 168 mg/dL → Acromegaly → bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with enlarging hands and coarse features is acromegaly: IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor 1)
  9. 52-year-old woman has numbness in both hands at night fatigue and 6 kg of weight gain cold intolerance, dry skin Delayed relaxation of ankle reflexes HR 56/min · BP 128/84 mm Hg → Hypothyroidism → bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with fatigue and weight gain is hypothyroidism: TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone)
  10. 60-year-old man on long-term hemodialysis for 12 years has numb hands at night both hands, thumb to middle finger, for months shoulder pain and stiffness No diabetes Afebrile · BP 138/80 mm Hg → β2-microglobulin amyloidosis → long-term hemodialysis with carpal tunnel syndrome is beta-2 microglobulin amyloidosis
  11. 58-year-old woman has 2 years of numbness of the thumb, index and middle fingers thenar atrophy weak thumb abduction Nerve conduction: severe median slowing at the wrist Afebrile · TSH normal → Carpal tunnel release → thenar atrophy means the nerve is losing motor fibers: skip conservative therapy and release the carpal tunnel
  12. 32-year-old woman, a new mother, has 4 weeks of radial wrist pain worse lifting her baby out of the crib tender over the radial styloid Finkelstein test positive Afebrile · no snuffbox tenderness → De Quervain tendinopathy → radial styloid tenderness with a positive Finkelstein test is de Quervain tendinopathy: a clinical diagnosis; thumb spica splint and an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug)
  13. 65-year-old woman has thumb base pain when opening jars squared appearance of the thumb base grind test positive Radiograph: joint space narrowing at the base of the thumb Afebrile · Finkelstein test negative → First CMC osteoarthritis → thumb base pain with a positive grind test in an older patient is first carpometacarpal (CMC) osteoarthritis
  14. 24-year-old woman, sexually active, has wrist tenosynovitis: painful swelling over both wrists migratory joint pains for 4 days a pustular rash: a few pustules on her forearms New partner last month T 38.4 °C · BP 112/70 mm Hg → Disseminated gonococcal infection → tenosynovitis, migratory arthralgia and pustules is disseminated gonococcal infection: nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT), blood cultures and ceftriaxone
  15. 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with de Quervain tendinopathy and is still in pain 6 weeks of a thumb spica splint and an NSAID Finkelstein test still positive No numbness Afebrile · no swelling over the snuffbox → Corticosteroid injection → after splint and NSAID fail, the next rung is a corticosteroid injection; release of the first dorsal compartment comes after that
  16. 40-year-old man, a competitive rower, has dorsal forearm pain worse with repetitive wrist extension crepitus a few centimeters proximal to the wrist with motion Radial styloid not tender Afebrile · Finkelstein test negative → Intersection syndrome → pain with crepitus about 4 cm proximal to the wrist in a rower is intersection syndrome
Transferable rule

A negative test cannot rule out disease when pretest probability is high, as with a D-dimer in high-probability pulmonary embolism; and when the diagnosis is clinical with a positive provocative test and no red flags, restraint is the answer.
